Triage (H13 healing; the filing seat explicitly left grading to triage): `pm:queue`, type Task. Commissioned as filed — a measurement with repairs, not a gate change: hand-adjudicate the 47 unread call sites in `packages/runtime/README.md`, repair what's wrong, **report defect count + denominator** so the A-vs-C decision on the remaining 73 sites is data-driven. Both fences carried verbatim: ⛔ no gate widening on this card; ⛔ option D (property-access receivers) not a rider — needs its own census first. Published-package README ⇒ changeset, not skip-changeset (PR #9906 precedent).

Size/model suggestion: M (47 adjudications), `mode:subagent`, opus.

## Ruling on the measurement this card commissioned: **the member-existence sweep is closed. Do not commission the other four documents.**

This card existed to produce one number and let it re-decide the sweep. It did. Ruling below, then the two things the number did not settle.

### The verdict

**1 of 30** documented members does not exist on the receiver's real type — 1 in 25 over the adjudicable subset — against a prior of 1 in 70. That is **one instance either way on a sample of 30**, which is not a material difference and does not support re-opening #9870's five-document sweep. The remaining ~73 unread sites stay unswept.

### ⚠️ My own card's denominator was wrong, and the provenance matters more than the correction

This card asserted **47 sites on 18 receivers**. The gate yields **30 on 17**. Five counting conventions were enumerated and none produces 47/18.

The traced cause is the sharp part: `47` is `derivedReceivers` — *"47 name(s) built from one"* — a **whole-repo scalar printed one line above** the `NOT read:` line on the same green output. The `domain:devx` seat wrote this card by transcribing a number from adjacent output that meant something else entirely.

That is precisely the defect class this repo has spent the day closing, committed by the seat commissioning the work. It is also why **#10815 is the right response** rather than an erratum: the gate prints whole-repo scalars and no per-document breakdown, so a reader who wants one document's figure has no option but to transcribe — and the two numbers sit on adjacent lines. Fixing the card would fix one instance; fixing the output closes the invitation.

The card's *argument* is unharmed: 30 is still ~3× the next-largest document (`packages/metadata/README.md`, 10), so the concentration reasoning that picked this document holds. Only the arithmetic moved.

### The finding that changes more than the verdict does

**5 of 30 sites are unadjudicable by anyone** — the receiver is a reader-owned illustrative object with no type anywhere, so neither a machine nor a human can answer the question. **1 in 6.**

That is more decision-relevant than the defect rate, and it argues the same direction: a hand read of the residual buys materially less coverage than its site count suggests. Any future proposal to sweep the remaining 73 should be priced against ~5/6 of them, not 73.

### ⛔ What I am NOT ruling on, and why

**2 of 30 name a real member with the wrong call shape** — `engine.update('user', user.id, …)` where the interface takes `(objectName, data, options?)` and identity resolves from a scalar `data.id` or `options.where.id`. Member-existence checking **cannot see these by construction**, so the 1-in-70 prior never priced them, and neither does the verdict above.

This is a **different class and a different sweep** from the one #9870 proposed. Ruling on it from n=2 in one document would repeat exactly the mistake this card's own scope gate was written to prevent — the same reasoning that declined option D pending a census. So: **not commissioned, and not declined either.** If anyone wants it, it needs a census of the class across the corpus first, and that census is its own card.

### On the work

The site list was derived from the gate's **own exports** rather than by grepping, and then **checksummed against it**: summed over all 60 published documents it reproduces the gate's printed `120 … 72` exactly, and tracks to `119 … 71` after the repairs. The limitation is stated rather than left implied — *"a whole-run checksum: it catches a systematic disagreement, not one document's worth."* That is the standard this round has been holding everyone to, applied unprompted to the instrument the dev built for itself.

The changeset is correct and was the trap on this card: `packages/runtime` is published, a README repair ships on npm, and PR #10365 previously got this right **against a dispatch instruction of mine that said otherwise**. This PR carries `.changeset/runtime-readme-unread-call-site-audit.md`.
